name: Klusio
author: klusio

sections.description:
Klusio helps small and medium sized businesses improve their visibility in Google and AI assistants. This plugin connects your existing WordPress site to your Klusio account and brings relevant proposals, drafts and results into WordPress.

The local Website check is free and works without a Klusio account. An account is required for the connected Growth workspace, proposals, drafts, measurements, chatbot and company knowledge. Installing the plugin alone does not connect your site, send content or publish anything.

Start with a useful improvement

The Klusio menu guides you through connecting your account, choosing an important page and reviewing a concrete proposal. Keep one focus page per administrator, inspect the real website and decide what to improve. Existing package, approval and publication rules remain in force.

Guided setup works from WordPress or your Klusio account. A WordPress administrator confirms the exact website and a Klusio account administrator confirms the account and permissions. The handshake is resumable and verifies both ends before storing a connection. A new connection starts with automatic publication off; reconnecting preserves your existing publication preferences.

Free website check without an account

Run a local inspection of up to 25 recently modified public pages and posts. Review heading gaps, images without descriptive alternatives, vague link text and configured indexing and HTTPS settings. Each finding links to the relevant WordPress editor. Builder coverage is explicitly partial; this check does not measure rankings, speed or the final frontend. It makes no external requests or automatic content changes. Weekly checks are optional and off by default. Connect an existing account or choose a Klusio plan when you want proposals, execution and shared Google and AI evidence.

Optional Measurements add a local page inventory and consent-aware form outcome counts. Sharing with the connected account is a separate choice. See the FAQ for coverage, consent and retention.

Page assistant and publication checks

Choose a page in Klusio > Pages. Preview and confirm a selected static text change in Gutenberg, Elementor or Bricks. Dynamic/shared fields stay in the native editor. Layout and unrelated content remain intact. Concurrent edits and active editor locks stop stale writes or restores; backups are verified before writing.

Internal links and per-use inline image descriptions can also be repaired locally without an account. Link suggestions cover up to 100 recent public pages with a time budget. Connected changes share account jobs and Growth history. Administrators can protect supported fields and add confirmed own project evidence, kept internal unless explicitly permitted as a content reference.

Public checks compare saved content, canonical URL, indexing instructions, images, recognizable dates and contact controls. Saved, publicly confirmed, indexed and delivered leads are separate facts. Use the existing browser inspection for mobile layout. Connected page saves schedule a bounded check through WordPress cron; hosting and traffic affect timing.

Your Klusio work inside WordPress

  • Overview: one prioritized next action, followed by the existing proposals, drafts and unresolved tasks. Connected workspaces read the current canonical account state. The read-only overview retains its visible synchronization time.
  • Growth: inspect the same execution contract as in your account. With explicit delegation, approve, reject or defer supported proposals and give feedback. Feedback pauses execution until a new approval.
  • Drafts: edit unpublished, unlinked articles, choose a local media image and update its alt text. Saving preserves a backup and invalidates the previous review. Publishing requires confirmation of the exact saved version.
  • Pages: find editable pages and posts, open their native editor and use “Improve with Klusio” for page-specific work. Deliberately saved visual feedback contains only the selected element description, short excerpt, note, viewport and page revision. It can become a manual improvement proposal in the same Growth queue; it does not change page content.
  • Chatbot: explicitly enable placement of your existing Klusio chat button, try a signed test conversation, edit the greeting, color and position, and inspect recent conversations, contact requests and recorded knowledge gaps. Existing widget installations are detected to avoid a second widget. Turning off plugin placement preserves manually installed code.
  • AI brain: edit the shared company profile and fixed answers, see available knowledge sources and writing-style status, and open the relevant account section for deeper management. Saving checks for concurrent edits and retains a verified before-state backup.
  • History: accepted work stays visible on the Klusio server when your browser closes. Repeated submissions do not create a second job; interrupted writes require inspection.
  • Settings: manage supported notification and work-mode preferences through the same authorized account services. Without a delegated settings scope, choices open an account confirmation screen.
  • Results: see registered changes, live verification, available Search Console comparisons and AI evidence. Retrieved search results, cited pages and actual company mentions remain separate. Missing measurements are never replaced with invented results.

The optional read-only overview displays its synchronization time. Account links preserve the selected page and require your account login.

Preserve your Elementor and Bricks website

Klusio can place approved changes in existing builder text fields, headings, buttons, FAQs and internal links. Layout, styling and unrelated content remain intact. Supported objects include Elementor pages, templates and global widgets, and Bricks pages, templates, headers, footers and global elements.

Before each write the plugin checks the page fingerprint and editing lock. If someone changed the page, it refuses to overwrite their work. It creates a compressed backup and WordPress revision, reads the result back and refreshes the affected page’s generated CSS and cache. Restore also checks for newer changes.

Supported query-loop additions use existing public post types, categories and approved text fields. Optional WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress operations preserve independently edited translations. Approved redirects apply only to genuinely missing addresses, so they do not hide existing pages or other plugins’ redirects. Existing Yoast and Rank Math page title and description routes remain compatible.

Preview the real theme and inspect mobile

Administrators can open an unpublished article as a separate private WordPress draft using the active theme. The saved account revision is the source. A new revision creates a new private copy; previous copies and local edits are retained. Featured images are shown when already present in the local media library; missing images are disclosed. Publish the canonical article from Klusio: these preview copies remain drafts while the plugin’s protection is active.

For existing pages and private previews, inspect the actual rendered frontend at desktop and mobile widths. A bounded browser check identifies possible overflow, strong image cropping, missing image alternatives, heading gaps, unnamed fields and missing next steps. Builders and templates participate through their rendered output. The check submits no forms and changes no page content.

Save dated observations with a page fingerprint and read them back in WordPress or your account. Earlier reports remain available locally. Changes to theme, templates or external content can still make an observation outdated. This is not a full accessibility, conversion or SEO audit. A separate collapsed check of stored text remains available.

Explicit connection and permissions

The optional work connection requires local consent and an active account administrator’s confirmation. Scopes separately allow reading, reviewing proposals, editing drafts, publishing/restoring and changing preferences. WordPress administrators can explicitly delegate supported actions to editors within the account grant. Chatbot access (including conversations and contact details) and AI-brain access are separate opt-in scopes. Existing grants receive neither automatically. Only administrators can place the frontend widget. Grants expire after 90 days and can be revoked. Changed integration credentials, website identity or account administrator access invalidate the delegation.

Honest evidence, controlled changes

Google comparisons show their sources, equal-length periods and data limitations. Low-data and later-change warnings remain visible. A difference after a change does not prove that the change caused it. Only explicitly successful live checks are presented as verified.

Complete before/after text is required for native on-page approval. Existing customer pages are not overwritten by the article draft editor. Destructive operations such as deleting or merging pages remain outside the proposal workflow. Installing or connecting alone adds no visitor tracking, advertising or unsolicited customer messages. The chatbot widget requires a separate explicit installation choice.

External services

The guided connection contacts https://klusio.nl/account/api/wordpress-connect.php only after you choose to check or confirm a connection. It exchanges a short-lived connection ticket, installation URL, account identity, chosen permissions and an automatically generated Application Password for the confirming WordPress administrator. That separate password is sent only in an HTTPS server-to-server request and stored encrypted in Klusio. The active plugin limits positively identified guided credentials to editorial REST routes; the underlying Application Password belongs to the administrator and must be revoked if that protection is no longer wanted. Account scopes separately limit actions initiated from the plugin. Revoke technical access in Users > Profile > Application Passwords. Revoke the account delegation in your Klusio account. No customer content is published by connecting.

This plugin is the WordPress part of the Klusio service (https://klusio.nl/). Without the guided connection or optional work connection, the plugin does not make external requests. The servers of Klusio connect to the REST API routes of this plugin on your website, authenticated with a separate WordPress application password created during guided setup or manually by your administrator.

With the optional work connection, WordPress sends authenticated HTTPS POST requests to https://klusio.nl/account/api/wordpress-native.php when an administrator opens live account data, submits an action or checks its status. Requests include the bound website, WordPress user ID, selected entity/action and any edited article text, media identifier, alt text, feedback or preferences needed for that action. A scoped credential is stored in a non-autoloaded WordPress option; only its hash is stored by Klusio. It is never placed in browser code or links. The endpoint does not accept arbitrary external destinations. Task history, feedback and verified before-state backups are retained by Klusio with the account; turning the connection off does not erase this audit history.

What is exchanged, and when:

  • When you connect or test the connection in your Klusio account, and before every change: Klusio reads the plugin status. That is the plugin version, which page builders are active, the capabilities of the connected user and a few recently edited Elementor or Bricks pages with their title and link. Without login, the status route only shows that the plugin is active, its version and its name.
  • When you approve a text change in Klusio: Klusio reads the page builder data of that page, sends back the changed data and reads it again to verify the result. Backups stay on your website.
  • When you ask Klusio to restore a change: Klusio sends which backup to restore.
  • When you publish a prepared blog article from Klusio (only after it was enabled on your site): Klusio sends the article address and a fingerprint of the approved version.
  • When you approve a redirect in Klusio: Klusio sends the old address and the new address on your website, and reads the list of redirects back to verify it. When you undo it, Klusio sends the old address to remove.

  • When you approve a translated page title or description in Klusio: Klusio sends the title or description of the page in your default language, the translation that your translated page shows and the approved new translation, and reads the dictionary entry back to verify it. When you undo it, Klusio sends which backup to restore.

  • When an administrator enables the optional account overview: Klusio sends the account identifier, connected site address, goal, selected proposal titles and descriptions, draft titles and bounded plain-text draft previews (up to 18,000 UTF-8 bytes each), proposal execution summaries, local page-draft references, work statuses, verification timestamps, available aggregate Search Console comparisons, six notification choices and the existing work mode through the existing authenticated WordPress connection. A bounded copy is stored as WordPress options. Short drafts may fit entirely in the preview; longer drafts are truncated and marked incomplete. No embedded media, financial information, account login tokens or visitor data are sent. Only the account and WordPress sender bound on the first successful synchronization may refresh it; a site administrator can reset that binding. No executable content is transferred.

  • Clicking a link to your Klusio account passes the website address and, where relevant, the selected page address or item ID. Prepared notification and work-mode choices are also passed to the account confirmation screen when you submit that form. These are navigation context only: Klusio still checks your login, company and access to that item.

Saved browser reviews contain the page address, revision fingerprint, observation time and bounded descriptions of elements needing inspection. Form values and visitor data are not collected. Reports remain in WordPress and are fetched by the bound Klusio account on request. Private article preview copies also remain in WordPress.

Chatbot access is optional and off in existing grants. With explicit chatbot permission, opening its screen retrieves up to 12 recent conversation summaries, up to 8 contact requests (names, email addresses and phone numbers), and up to 12 knowledge-gap topics from the connected Klusio account. Opening a conversation retrieves at most its last 100 messages. They are shown to authorized users, not copied to a persistent WordPress conversation database. AI-brain permission allows editing the shared company profile and up to 50 displayed fixed answers through the existing knowledge service. Optional gap-to-proposal actions also require the drafts permission.

Placing the widget is a separate WordPress administrator action. It stores the existing public embed identifier locally and loads https://klusio.nl/embed.js on the frontend. The widget then communicates with Klusio backend/API endpoints using the existing chatbot privacy and consent settings. Visitor messages and voluntarily submitted contact information are processed by the Klusio service as described in its privacy policy. Disabling plugin placement stops the plugin from adding that script; clear page caches and separately remove any earlier manual embed if needed. A signed, short-lived test conversation uses the existing test mode, suppressing visitor records, contact requests and notifications. Test calls can use the existing AI service. Test credentials expire and the preview stops sending requests before expiry.

Klusio terms and conditions: https://klusio.nl/algemene-voorwaarden/
Klusio privacy policy: https://klusio.nl/privacy/

Can I use the plugin without a Klusio account?

Yes. The local website check examines stored content from up to 25 recently modified public pages and posts for heading jumps, empty image descriptions and vague link text. It does not send content to Klusio or use AI. Private and password-protected pages are excluded. Builder and dynamic content checks are explicitly partial; this is not a rendered-site, performance, indexing or ranking audit. Run it manually or explicitly enable a weekly WordPress cron check. The last four reports remain in WordPress. Connecting a Klusio account is optional and gives access to the shared growth workflow and measurements.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins, Add New, search for “Klusio”, then install and activate it. You can also upload the zip file under Plugins, Add New, Upload Plugin.
  2. Open Klusio in your WordPress admin and choose Connect my Klusio account. If you do not have an account, use Start with Klusio and return to this tab after signing up.
  3. In Klusio, confirm the installation address and choose the account permissions. Return to WordPress, check the account name and confirm. The plugin creates separate access, tests it and loads your overview. No password copying is needed.
  4. You can also begin at WordPress in your Klusio account. Existing publication settings stay unchanged. A new connection has automatic forwarding disabled until you choose otherwise.

Advanced manual setup remains available in the account’s technical connection settings. Use a separate WordPress application password, test and save the connection. Never use your ordinary login password.
sections.faq:
Which optional website measurements are collected?

Measurements are off by default. Administrators can enable a local inventory of up to 500 public, unprotected posts and pages, processed in small cron batches. Coverage is limited to supported saved main content; templates, menus and dynamic content are not fully measured.

Mapped Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WPForms and Bricks forms can record separate server-confirmed outcomes: stored, processed, mail accepted or mail failed. This requires an active WP Consent API integration in opt-in mode and the visitor’s statistics consent. Logged-in users are excluded. No field contents, IP addresses, email addresses, visitor profiles or tracking cookies are collected. Local daily totals are retained for 90 days. Counts are partial and do not prove inbox delivery, unique leads or revenue.

Sharing is a separate administrator choice bound to the exact connected account. Klusio periodically retrieves the inventory and the last 30 complete UTC days of mapped aggregate totals over the authenticated connection. It may suggest at most three manual checks, with source and coverage, in the existing Growth workspace. Counts are never added to Google Analytics totals. Reconnecting requires renewed sharing consent. No account is required for local inspections. Klusio privacy policy: https://klusio.nl/privacy-policy/.

How is technical access restricted?

The Connection screen checks WordPress and Klusio in both directions and shows scopes, expiry and the last received overview. New Application Passwords created through guided setup, and exact credentials identified from that setup, are restricted by the active plugin to supported editorial REST routes. User administration, plugin/theme management, general settings, batch calls and unrelated routes are blocked for those credentials. Normal administrator sessions and other integrations remain unchanged.

This technical restriction depends on the plugin staying active. Revoke the Application Password in WordPress to remove access independently. Older manual credentials are not silently changed; reconnect through guided setup to create a limited credential. Account scopes further limit operations initiated in the plugin. No account browser session or login token is shared with WordPress.

Does Klusio change my pages without my approval?

No. Klusio only writes a change you approved in your Klusio account. The plugin refuses any write that does not match the version Klusio read before.

What happens if someone edits the page at the same time?

Nothing is written. When a page is open in the WordPress or page builder editor, or changed since Klusio read it, the plugin refuses the change and keeps the current version.

Where are the backups stored?

On your own website, as compressed post meta of the page (up to three per page), next to a normal WordPress revision.

How do I undo a change?

Choose restore in your Klusio account, or use the WordPress revisions of the page.

Why is the page data sent as base64?

Elementor data contains HTML. Hosting firewalls sometimes block requests that contain HTML, and many limit the size of a request. The data is therefore sent compressed and base64 encoded. It is data, never code: the plugin decodes it, checks that it is valid page builder data and stores it as post meta.

Can I use the plugin as a must-use plugin?

Yes. Place klusio-builder-bridge.php in wp-content/mu-plugins. A must-use plugin is not updated by WordPress, so a regular install is recommended. When both are present, the must-use copy loads first. To migrate, back up the must-use file, install and activate the regular plugin, then move the old must-use file out of its loading directory and verify the connection. Keep the backup until verification succeeds. Klusio provides a guided migration for supported sites.

Which data does the public status route show?

The status route shows that the plugin is active, its version and its name. The guided setup connect-info route additionally shows the public WordPress installation URL. Neither proves access. Pairing proof requires authentication with the exact newly generated application password. All customer data requires authorization.

How do I stop Klusio from releasing blog drafts?

Releasing blog drafts is off by default. A user who may publish posts can switch it off again with a POST request to /wp-json/klusio/v1/blog-release with enabled=false, or by deactivating the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.24.0

  • Optional bounded website inventory and consent-aware mapped form outcome aggregates.
  • Separate local collection and exact-account sharing choices, default off.
  • Shared measurement quality and evidence-based manual Growth proposals without duplicate Analytics counts.

1.23.0

  • Added a page assistant for selected static Gutenberg, Elementor and Bricks fields, with exact previews, explicit confirmation, preserved design and guarded restore.
  • Added local internal-link and per-use image-description repairs, including a bounded, dated link inventory.
  • Connected changes share durable account jobs and Growth registration. Public completion requires evidence of the exact selected effect, not only an HTTP 200 response.
  • Added separate public-page checks and shared history in WordPress and Klusio, field protection and confirmed project references.
  • Preserved existing scopes, onboarding, drafts, chatbot and company knowledge. Installation does not grant new permissions or alter customer content.

1.22.1

  • Render the bundled official Klusio icon through the WordPress-supported inline SVG menu route.
  • Clarify that the local Website check needs no account, while connected work does.

1.22.0

  • Free local website checks without an account, with explicit coverage and optional weekly WordPress checks. Content stays on your site.
  • Paginated chatbot conversations, actual visitor questions and dated activity from the same Klusio account.
  • Clear brand-color controls and a real private chatbot preview instead of a simulated header. Validate input before saving.
  • Official Klusio menu icon, calmer labels and improved mobile spacing.

1.21.0

  • Add optional native Chatbot and AI-brain screens with shared canonical data, separate explicit permissions and protected saves.
  • Add opt-in frontend placement, duplicate detection and temporary test conversations.
  • Show source counts, fixed answers, recent conversations and leads, and controlled proposals from knowledge gaps.

1.20.0

  • A focused action inbox uses the existing Growth queue, drafts and unresolved tasks. Execution readiness distinguishes account permissions, customer work and reviewed automatic steps.
  • Point to an actual element in a private theme preview, save a deliberate annotation and create the same improvement proposal in Klusio. Stored page revisions prevent stale feedback being presented as current; annotations are recoverable and never edit the page.
  • Shared Google before/after visuals and separate AI evidence counts retain dates, source, sample limitations and the underlying values.
  • Compact mobile navigation, accessible controls, clearer action hierarchy and less duplicated page evidence.

1.19.0

  • Turn saved desktop/mobile observations into specific Groeimotor work plans. Website-editor work is clearly distinguished from executable changes.
  • Automatically preserve text workcopies across WordPress and Klusio, with explicit comparison before resuming and protection against concurrent edits.
  • Plan or cancel an approved article in the shared Klusio calendar. Current content and delegated permissions are rechecked before publication.
  • Private theme previews can securely import the current featured photo without changing shared media descriptions.
  • Compare actual sanitized page snapshots side by side on desktop/mobile. Unlocated changes remain explicitly unverified.
  • Administrators can delegate reading, drafting, decisions and publication separately to existing WordPress editors. Revocation stops queued work.

1.18.0

  • Check desktop and mobile together, then jump from an observation to the relevant element in your actual website preview.
  • Saved checks update the page overview immediately. Unfinished checks are protected when leaving the screen.
  • Main-content conversion checks, missing label references and unloaded images are clearer; broken or changed previews cannot be saved as current.
  • The first-improvement guide retains your selected page. Existing page content and customer edits remain unchanged.

1.17.0

  • Guided first improvement with an important page, actionable checks and separate publication approval.
  • Private article previews in the real WordPress theme; saved account revisions use separate copies and preserve local edits.
  • Desktop and mobile rendered-page checks with dated findings, retained previous reports and shared account evidence.
  • Round-trip connection health, expiry and explicit account permissions. Guided application passwords are restricted to editorial and Klusio routes while the plugin is active.
  • One page story across WordPress and Klusio: proposals, changes, live verification and comparable Google/AI evidence.

1.16.0

  • Guided connection from WordPress and the Klusio account, with explicit consent on both sides and no manual password copying.
  • A separate WordPress Application Password is transmitted server-to-server over HTTPS, never in browser URLs or pages.
  • Existing publication preferences and website content are preserved. New connections start with automatic forwarding disabled.
  • Recoverable confirmation, short-lived tickets, exact website/account binding, concurrency checks and verified connection backups.

1.15.0

  • Optional scoped WordPress work connection with explicit consent on both sides, revocation and expiry.
  • Native proposal decisions, feedback and defer; complete text comparisons and protected restore.
  • Article draft editing, media selection and matching alt text; saved-version review before publication.
  • Native page draft workflow, preferences, persistent task history and per-page Google/AI evidence.
  • Existing builder layout, customer edits, package checks and ordinary WordPress updates are preserved.

1.14.2

  • Refined workspace spacing, left-aligned navigation, consistent icons and neutral card borders.
  • All existing account permissions, approval steps and builder protection remain unchanged.

1.14.1

  • Clarify the existing bounded draft previews in the service data disclosure and the coverage of static builder checks.
  • No additional data access or publishing permissions.

1.14.0

  • Read draft article text and the existing proposal execution plan directly in WordPress.
  • Search local pages, inspect bounded editorial checks and open native editors and previews without leaving WordPress.
  • Open mapped full-page drafts in the current website layout, respecting local edit capabilities.
  • Explicitly distinguish incomplete, dynamic and builder content checks from a full website audit.
  • Extended previews use the existing opt-in, tenant binding, freshness checks and bounded authenticated synchronization. No new outbound requests or publication permissions.

1.13.0

  • Added a responsive Klusio sidebar with overview, growth, drafts, results, settings and connection.
  • Added guided setup for new accounts and existing accounts that have not connected their website.
  • Show existing internal-link and conversion actions with their evidence and exact account destinations.
  • Show available verified page measurements with source, dates and uncertainty.
  • Prepare notification and work-mode choices in WordPress and confirm them securely in the Klusio account.

1.12.0

  • Adds an optional WordPress workspace with overview, growth proposals, local and Klusio drafts, and page-specific links to the Klusio account.
  • Requires administrator opt-in for account summaries, restricts access by capability and preserves existing content and publication settings.
  • Uses the existing authenticated connection, bounded snapshots and explicit freshness indicators. The plugin makes no outbound service requests.

1.11.2

  • The public plugin name is now Klusio. Existing connections, plugin paths and the WordPress update channel are preserved.

1.11.1

  • Creating list items and new translations respects the post type’s separate create_posts capability. Existing translations remain editable with the appropriate edit permissions.

1.11.0

  • Usage lookups are cached per user and recheck page access on every cached response. Template condition titles also respect page access.
  • Layout size is checked before decoding and before TranslatePress inspection, for raw, base64 and compressed requests.
  • Translations are supplied by WordPress.org language packs. Updates use the standard WordPress.org mechanism for regular installations.

1.10.0

  • TranslatePress: Klusio can place an approved page title and meta description for the translated version of a page or post. TranslatePress translates them as texts of the page; the new translation is stored as a reviewed translation in one transaction, only when the translated page still shows the translation Klusio read. The rows it replaces are kept as a backup on your site (up to 200), and restoring brings them back unless someone changed the translation since. A title or description that is also a heading or text of the page is refused. The caches of the page in both languages are refreshed. The backups are removed when the plugin is deleted.

1.9.0

  • Redirects for addresses that give a 404: Klusio can store a redirect that you approved, from an old address on your website to another address on your website (301). It is only used when WordPress finds nothing at that address, so it never hides an existing page, post, product or a redirect made with another plugin. No chains, never from the home page, the admin, the login or the REST API, and only by a user who may edit and publish all pages. Every change carries a fingerprint of the list Klusio read; the list is removed when the plugin is deleted.
  • The status (with login) reports the number of redirects and whether the connected user may manage them.

1.8.0

  • Multilingual sites (WPML or Polylang): Klusio can place the translation of a blog post as its own post in that language, linked to the original. It gets the featured image of the original, the translated categories and tags that exist, and the meta description in Yoast SEO or Rank Math. The address comes from the multilingual plugin. A translation that someone made on the site itself is never overwritten.
  • TranslatePress: Klusio can add the translation of a blog post to the dictionary. A sentence that TranslatePress splits at bold text or a link is stored as one translation block, so it is translated as a whole; the block is only kept when TranslatePress recognizes it. Translations made or corrected by hand stay as they are; an automatic translation may be replaced by the checked one. Klusio may update a translation it stored itself, as long as nobody changed it in TranslatePress; the list of those translations is removed when the plugin is deleted.
  • The status (with login) reports the multilingual plugin (WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, Weglot or GTranslate), the default language and the active languages.

1.7.0

  • Lists that a page shows with a query loop (Bricks): Klusio can add an approved item, such as a frequently asked question that is a post of its own with the answer in an ACF text field and the category of the page. The item gets a key from Klusio; restoring moves only that item to the trash. The page cache of the page that shows the list is refreshed.

1.6.1

  • Restoring the alt text of an image on a bilingual site keeps existing translations and leaves an untranslated text untranslated.
  • Alt text of an image without a bilingual setup (/klusio/v1/media/<id>/alt): the pages that show the image get fresh caches, so the new description is visible right away. Elementor kept the old one when only WordPress changed it.

1.6.0

  • Bilingual sites (TranslatePress): existing translations are chosen exactly as TranslatePress shows them (first translation for the exact original), instead of refusing the page when the dictionary holds duplicates or case variants.
  • New sections may contain images, icon lists, image boxes, spacers, dividers and icons; texts and image alt texts are translated together with the page.
  • Alt text of an image in both languages together (new route, inspect first, one transaction).
  • A refused bilingual change returns a short reason code for the support team.

1.5.0

  • All messages in English, with a Dutch translation included.
  • Releasing blog drafts that Klusio prepared is now a setting per site, enabled for one Klusio account by a user who may publish posts (/klusio/v1/blog-release). The routes are /klusio/v1/blog/<id>/publish and /klusio/v1/blog/<id>/preview.
  • The enabled setting is removed when the plugin is deleted.

1.4.2

  • Release of a blog draft prepared by Klusio, with an exact check of text, layout and address before publishing.

1.4.1

  • Stronger rollback backups for changes in two languages.

1.4.0

  • Saves the source language and its TranslatePress translation together, with a rollback when one of them fails.

1.3.2

  • Byte exact atomic changes and restores for both page builders, including Bricks headers, footers and global elements. A conflict never overwrites a newer version.

1.3.1

  • Bricks CSS is regenerated only with recognised parameters; a shared Elementor block refreshes the CSS per page.

1.3.0

  • Bricks support: pages, headers, footers, templates and global elements.

1.2.0

  • Templates and global widgets, usage lookup, compressed backups (up to three per page).

1.1.0

  • First version: Klusio updates texts on Elementor pages without touching the design.

It makes no external requests or automatic content changes. Weekly checks are optional and off by default. Connect an existing account or choose a Klusio plan when you want proposals, execution and shared Google and AI evidence.

Optional Measurements add a local page inventory and consent-aware form outcome counts. Sharing with the connected account is a separate choice. See the FAQ for coverage, consent and retention.

Page assistant and publication checks

Choose a page in Klusio > Pages. Preview and confirm a selected static text change in Gutenberg, Elementor or Bricks. Dynamic/shared fields stay in the native editor. Layout and unrelated content remain intact. Concurrent edits and active editor locks stop stale writes or restores; backups are verified before writing.

Internal links and per-use inline image descriptions can also be repaired locally without an account. Link suggestions cover up to 100 recent public pages with a time budget. Connected changes share account jobs and Growth history. Administrators can protect supported fields and add confirmed own project evidence, kept internal unless explicitly permitted as a content reference.

Public checks compare saved content, canonical URL, indexing instructions, images, recognizable dates and contact controls. Saved, publicly confirmed, indexed and delivered leads are separate facts. Use the existing browser inspection for mobile layout. Connected page saves schedule a bounded check through WordPress cron; hosting and traffic affect timing.

Your Klusio work inside WordPress

  • Overview: one prioritized next action, followed by the existing proposals, drafts and unresolved tasks. Connected workspaces read the current canonical account state. The read-only overview retains its visible synchronization time.
  • Growth: inspect the same execution contract as in your account. With explicit delegation, approve, reject or defer supported proposals and give feedback. Feedback pauses execution until a new approval.
  • Drafts: edit unpublished, unlinked articles, choose a local media image and update its alt text. Saving preserves a backup and invalidates the previous review. Publishing requires confirmation of the exact saved version.
  • Pages: find editable pages and posts, open their native editor and use “Improve with Klusio” for page-specific work. Deliberately saved visual feedback contains only the selected element description, short excerpt, note, viewport and page revision. It can become a manual improvement proposal in the same Growth queue; it does not change page content.
  • Chatbot: explicitly enable placement of your existing Klusio chat button, try a signed test conversation, edit the greeting, color and position, and inspect recent conversations, contact requests and recorded knowledge gaps. Existing widget installations are detected to avoid a second widget. Turning off plugin placement preserves manually installed code.
  • AI brain: edit the shared company profile and fixed answers, see available knowledge sources and writing-style status, and open the relevant account section for deeper management. Saving checks for concurrent edits and retains a verified before-state backup.
  • History: accepted work stays visible on the Klusio server when your browser closes. Repeated submissions do not create a second job; interrupted writes require inspection.
  • Settings: manage supported notification and work-mode preferences through the same authorized account services. Without a delegated settings scope, choices open an account confirmation screen.
  • Results: see registered changes, live verification, available Search Console comparisons and AI evidence. Retrieved search results, cited pages and actual company mentions remain separate. Missing measurements are never replaced with invented results.

The optional read-only overview displays its synchronization time. Account links preserve the selected page and require your account login.

Preserve your Elementor and Bricks website

Klusio can place approved changes in existing builder text fields, headings, buttons, FAQs and internal links. Layout, styling and unrelated content remain intact. Supported objects include Elementor pages, templates and global widgets, and Bricks pages, templates, headers, footers and global elements.

Before each write the plugin checks the page fingerprint and editing lock. If someone changed the page, it refuses to overwrite their work. It creates a compressed backup and WordPress revision, reads the result back and refreshes the affected page’s generated CSS and cache. Restore also checks for newer changes.

Supported query-loop additions use existing public post types, categories and approved text fields. Optional WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress operations preserve independently edited translations. Approved redirects apply only to genuinely missing addresses, so they do not hide existing pages or other plugins’ redirects. Existing Yoast and Rank Math page title and description routes remain compatible.

Preview the real theme and inspect mobile

Administrators can open an unpublished article as a separate private WordPress draft using the active theme. The saved account revision is the source. A new revision creates a new private copy; previous copies and local edits are retained. Featured images are shown when already present in the local media library; missing images are disclosed. Publish the canonical article from Klusio: these preview copies remain drafts while the plugin’s protection is active.

For existing pages and private previews, inspect the actual rendered frontend at desktop and mobile widths. A bounded browser check identifies possible overflow, strong image cropping, missing image alternatives, heading gaps, unnamed fields and missing next steps. Builders and templates participate through their rendered output. The check submits no forms and changes no page content.

Save dated observations with a page fingerprint and read them back in WordPress or your account. Earlier reports remain available locally. Changes to theme, templates or external content can still make an observation outdated. This is not a full accessibility, conversion or SEO audit. A separate collapsed check of stored text remains available.

Explicit connection and permissions

The optional work connection requires local consent and an active account administrator’s confirmation. Scopes separately allow reading, reviewing proposals, editing drafts, publishing/restoring and changing preferences. WordPress administrators can explicitly delegate supported actions to editors within the account grant. Chatbot access (including conversations and contact details) and AI-brain access are separate opt-in scopes. Existing grants receive neither automatically. Only administrators can place the frontend widget. Grants expire after 90 days and can be revoked. Changed integration credentials, website identity or account administrator access invalidate the delegation.

Honest evidence, controlled changes

Google comparisons show their sources, equal-length periods and data limitations. Low-data and later-change warnings remain visible. A difference after a change does not prove that the change caused it. Only explicitly successful live checks are presented as verified.

Complete before/after text is required for native on-page approval. Existing customer pages are not overwritten by the article draft editor. Destructive operations such as deleting or merging pages remain outside the proposal workflow. Installing or connecting alone adds no visitor tracking, advertising or unsolicited customer messages. The chatbot widget requires a separate explicit installation choice.

External services

The guided connection contacts https://klusio.nl/account/api/wordpress-connect.php only after you choose to check or confirm a connection. It exchanges a short-lived connection ticket, installation URL, account identity, chosen permissions and an automatically generated Application Password for the confirming WordPress administrator. That separate password is sent only in an HTTPS server-to-server request and stored encrypted in Klusio. The active plugin limits positively identified guided credentials to editorial REST routes; the underlying Application Password belongs to the administrator and must be revoked if that protection is no longer wanted. Account scopes separately limit actions initiated from the plugin. Revoke technical access in Users > Profile > Application Passwords. Revoke the account delegation in your Klusio account. No customer content is published by connecting.

This plugin is the WordPress part of the Klusio service (https://klusio.nl/). Without the guided connection or optional work connection, the plugin does not make external requests. The servers of Klusio connect to the REST API routes of this plugin on your website, authenticated with a separate WordPress application password created during guided setup or manually by your administrator.

With the optional work connection, WordPress sends authenticated HTTPS POST requests to https://klusio.nl/account/api/wordpress-native.php when an administrator opens live account data, submits an action or checks its status. Requests include the bound website, WordPress user ID, selected entity/action and any edited article text, media identifier, alt text, feedback or preferences needed for that action. A scoped credential is stored in a non-autoloaded WordPress option; only its hash is stored by Klusio. It is never placed in browser code or links. The endpoint does not accept arbitrary external destinations. Task history, feedback and verified before-state backups are retained by Klusio with the account; turning the connection off does not erase this audit history.

What is exchanged, and when:

  • When you connect or test the connection in your Klusio account, and before every change: Klusio reads the plugin status. That is the plugin version, which page builders are active, the capabilities of the connected user and a few recently edited Elementor or Bricks pages with their title and link. Without login, the status route only shows that the plugin is active, its version and its name.
  • When you approve a text change in Klusio: Klusio reads the page builder data of that page, sends back the changed data and reads it again to verify the result. Backups stay on your website.
  • When you ask Klusio to restore a change: Klusio sends which backup to restore.
  • When you publish a prepared blog article from Klusio (only after it was enabled on your site): Klusio sends the article address and a fingerprint of the approved version.
  • When you approve a redirect in Klusio: Klusio sends the old address and the new address on your website, and reads the list of redirects back to verify it. When you undo it, Klusio sends the old address to remove.

  • When you approve a translated page title or description in Klusio: Klusio sends the title or description of the page in your default language, the translation that your translated page shows and the approved new translation, and reads the dictionary entry back to verify it. When you undo it, Klusio sends which backup to restore.

  • When an administrator enables the optional account overview: Klusio sends the account identifier, connected site address, goal, selected proposal titles and descriptions, draft titles and bounded plain-text draft previews (up to 18,000 UTF-8 bytes each), proposal execution summaries, local page-draft references, work statuses, verification timestamps, available aggregate Search Console comparisons, six notification choices and the existing work mode through the existing authenticated WordPress connection. A bounded copy is stored as WordPress options. Short drafts may fit entirely in the preview; longer drafts are truncated and marked incomplete. No embedded media, financial information, account login tokens or visitor data are sent. Only the account and WordPress sender bound on the first successful synchronization may refresh it; a site administrator can reset that binding. No executable content is transferred.

  • Clicking a link to your Klusio account passes the website address and, where relevant, the selected page address or item ID. Prepared notification and work-mode choices are also passed to the account confirmation screen when you submit that form. These are navigation context only: Klusio still checks your login, company and access to that item.

Saved browser reviews contain the page address, revision fingerprint, observation time and bounded descriptions of elements needing inspection. Form values and visitor data are not collected. Reports remain in WordPress and are fetched by the bound Klusio account on request. Private article preview copies also remain in WordPress.

Chatbot access is optional and off in existing grants. With explicit chatbot permission, opening its screen retrieves up to 12 recent conversation summaries, up to 8 contact requests (names, email addresses and phone numbers), and up to 12 knowledge-gap topics from the connected Klusio account. Opening a conversation retrieves at most its last 100 messages. They are shown to authorized users, not copied to a persistent WordPress conversation database. AI-brain permission allows editing the shared company profile and up to 50 displayed fixed answers through the existing knowledge service. Optional gap-to-proposal actions also require the drafts permission.

Placing the widget is a separate WordPress administrator action. It stores the existing public embed identifier locally and loads https://klusio.nl/embed.js on the frontend. The widget then communicates with Klusio backend/API endpoints using the existing chatbot privacy and consent settings. Visitor messages and voluntarily submitted contact information are processed by the Klusio service as described in its privacy policy. Disabling plugin placement stops the plugin from adding that script; clear page caches and separately remove any earlier manual embed if needed. A signed, short-lived test conversation uses the existing test mode, suppressing visitor records, contact requests and notifications. Test calls can use the existing AI service. Test credentials expire and the preview stops sending requests before expiry.

Klusio terms and conditions: https://klusio.nl/algemene-voorwaarden/
Klusio privacy policy: https://klusio.nl/privacy/

Can I use the plugin without a Klusio account?

Yes. The local website check examines stored content from up to 25 recently modified public pages and posts for heading jumps, empty image descriptions and vague link text. It does not send content to Klusio or use AI. Private and password-protected pages are excluded. Builder and dynamic content checks are explicitly partial; this is not a rendered-site, performance, indexing or ranking audit. Run it manually or explicitly enable a weekly WordPress cron check. The last four reports remain in WordPress. Connecting a Klusio account is optional and gives access to the shared growth workflow and measurements.
